traits.stem_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Peniocereus: Peniocereus: shrubs, low, erect to sprawling, arching or scrambling, sparingly branched; roots turnip-shaped; stems gray, gray-green, greenish brown, brown or purplish, columnar, slender, rigid, canescent; ribs often prominent; areoles circular to elliptic, lanose; spines 1.5-4 mm, radial and central spines similar. Flowers nocturnal, usually borne laterally along the distal portions of the ribs, salverform with a long tube flaring abruptly near the apex; ovary with low tubercles, spiny, areoles woolly. Fruits red to scarlet, fleshy, low tuberculate, scaleless, spiny; floral remnant persistent. Radials and centrals alike, so all are counted as radials; the stem tips taper by eye from the illustration.
